plot_route: Climb off trail from the drainage before Buck Creek Bridge and bushwack/create a trail through dense manzanita and other shrubs
general_plot_notes: Approach was horrific--we attempted walking up the creek, but hit waterfalls. We bushwacked and sawed our way through manzanita, and eventually discovered a coute up a drainage with a relatively short bushwhack. JEC scouted original point to within 30m, and found 2 live and 1 dead PILA. However, this point was way too far from our camp at Buck Creek as it took the whole day to get there given the dense shrub cover. Although the site had PILA, it was not feasible to read a plot and travel there from the nearest possible campsite in a single day. Too far and PILA was similarly sparse. Shifted the plot to the saddle (flat with some trees on the East and West side of the saddle) and satelite grove (more similar east aspect like the original point) to keep the day trips from Buck Creek humanly possible. 5 PILA seedlings in the full plot, more PIJE and many more CADE and ABCO seedlings and saplings too, but no formal count due to the large/balloon nature of the plot and time constraints with only 2 people. Lots of PILA regen (seedlings and saplings) near the satelite clump plus a few in between the main transect and the satelite portion of the plot. Only one of these was measured to check if it was coreable (14 DBH). No fire scar on trees, but area has lots of dead and down, including some PILA on the saddle. Evidence of charred stumps and burned logs, so perhaps an older fire than expected based on the imagery that suggested a fire in 2021 or the fire was really patchy.
